question: After credentialed lifecycle proof passes, should Crabbox ship this direct provider with persistent Codespaces-capable GitHub credentials, operator billing exposure, and default deletion of claim-owned Codespaces?
rationale: Source and tests can establish the intended ownership mechanics, but only maintainers can accept the permanent credential, cost, operational-support, and destructive-resource boundary.

options.title: Prove and accept direct lifecycle
options.body: Require redacted exact-head create, run, SSH, dirty-retain, and confirmed-delete proof, then ship the documented direct provider contract.

options.title: Adopt a retain-first default
options.body: Require remote deletion to be explicitly enabled through trusted configuration while stop-and-retain remains the default behavior.

options.title: Pause provider adoption
options.body: Do not land the provider until credentials, quota, recurring smoke ownership, and retained-resource recovery responsibility are assigned.

recommendation.title: Prove and accept direct lifecycle
recommendation.body: Require redacted exact-head create, run, SSH, dirty-retain, and confirmed-delete proof, then ship the documented direct provider contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They carried the major lifecycle-safety repairs and current-head integration, making them the strongest available owner for the final boundary decision.
